overview: Swadesh Darshan Scheme 2.0 is a centrally sponsored scheme launched by the Ministry of Tourism, Government of India, aimed at developing theme-based tourist circuits across the country. It focuses on integrated development of tourism infrastructure, promoting sustainable and responsible tourism, and enhancing visitor experience through planned interventions. The scheme supports the creation of world-class tourism destinations by improving connectivity, facilities, and services at identified circuits.
objectives: Develop theme-based tourist circuits in a planned and prioritized manner
Enhance tourism infrastructure and visitor facilities at identified destinations
Promote sustainable and responsible tourism practices
Increase domestic and international tourist footfalls
Generate employment opportunities through tourism-led economic growth
Preserve and promote cultural and natural heritage
Strengthen linkages between tourism and other sectors like handicrafts, local cuisine, and adventure sports
eligibility: State Governments and Union Territory Administrations are eligible to submit project proposals under the Swadesh Darshan Scheme 2.0. Projects must be aligned with the identified thematic circuits and adhere to the scheme guidelines, including norms for sustainable tourism, environmental clearances, and land availability.
benefits: Financial assistance for development of tourism infrastructure such as wayside amenities, tourist centers, accommodation, eco-lodges, sound & light shows, pathways, landscaping, illumination, and signage. Non-financial benefits include technical support from the Ministry of Tourism, convergence with other central and state schemes, and promotion of identified circuits through marketing and branding initiatives.
financial_support: The scheme provides central financial assistance (CFA) to State Governments and Union Territory Administrations for the development of tourism infrastructure in identified circuits. The funding pattern is 60:40 for general category states (Centre:State), 90:10 for North Eastern and Himalayan states, and 100% central funding for Union Territories. The assistance is released in installments based on physical and financial progress of the project.
application_process: 1. State Governments/UT Administrations identify potential tourist circuits based on thematic themes. 2. Prepare Detailed Project Reports (DPRs) as per scheme guidelines. 3. Submit proposals to the Ministry of Tourism along with required documents. 4. Proposals are appraised by the Project Appraisal Committee (PAC). 5. Upon approval, sanction letters are issued. 6. Funds are released in installments subject to utilization-linked manner. 7. Projects are monitored through site visits and progress reports.
implementing_agency: Ministry of Tourism, Government of India
caveats: Projects must be completed within the stipulated timeline as per sanction
Beneficiary states/UTs must bear the prescribed share of project cost
Utilization certificates and progress reports are mandatory for subsequent fund releases
Land must be free from encumbrances and clear title must be available
No financial assistance for recurring expenses or manpower
